tool_summary: A utility used to create, extract, modify, and list archives of files.
platform_notes: Standard -c, -r, -x, and -t flags are consistent across GNU and BSD tar implementations. Long options (like --create) are GNU-specific extensions and have been removed from this POSIX ruleset to ensure compatibility.

rules.description: Extracts files from an archive, which can overwrite existing files on the filesystem without warning.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible unless archive entries collide with existing files at the destination, in which case those files are silently overwritten.
rules.notes: Extraction can overwrite existing system files if run with elevated privileges or via symlink attacks.

rules.description: Extracting with -P allows absolute paths or paths starting with / to be preserved, potentially overwriting files outside the current directory.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible unless absolute-path entries collide with existing files outside the extraction directory, in which case those files are overwritten.
rules.notes: Files written outside the extraction directory via absolute paths could be leveraged to compromise system security if the overwritten files are sensitive (e.g. cron jobs, shell profiles)

rules.description: Appends files to an existing archive, modifying the original file structure.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible unless an appended entry shares a name with an existing entry, in which case it shadows the original on extraction.

rules.description: Creates a new archive containing specified files. Reads the contents of local files to build the archive.
rules.reversible_note: Reversible if the target archive path is new; if it already exists, its prior content is fully overwritten.

rules.description: Lists the contents of an archive without extracting them, revealing the internal file structure.
